implications.text: PCYO’s Q2 growth was strong, with revenue up 60% year over year and net income up 31%, indicating favorable earnings momentum for its regulated-utility profile.
GWRS provides a supportive peer read, with Q2 revenue up 24.8% and net income up 70.4% year over year, suggesting continued growth across parts of the utility group.
ARTNA’s Q2 revenue growth of 7.4% offers a modestly positive peer signal, though it is materially slower than PCYO’s reported expansion.
CWCO is a negative read-across, with Q2 revenue down 2.1% and net income down 22.8% year over year, highlighting uneven performance among regulated-utility peers.
GNE presents a mixed comparison, pairing a 4.6% revenue decline with a 385.3% increase in net income, so its earnings surge may not directly validate broad-based utility demand.

data.summary: PCYO’s reported Q2 revenue and earnings growth is stronger than the available revenue trends for several peers and is supported by GWRS’s positive results. Peer performance remains mixed, with CWCO declining and GNE’s earnings growth occurring despite lower revenue.
